newsitem.title: USA: Pediatricians say care overrides religious beliefs.
newsitem.headline: Pediatricians say care overrides religious beliefs.

text.p: Children should not be denied medical care regardless of the parents' religious beliefs and states should ensure that parents are held legally accountable if harm comes to a child, a pediatricians' group said Monday.

"Constitutional guarantees of freedom of religion do not permit children to be harmed through religious practices, nor do they allow religion to be a defense when an individual harms or neglects a child," the policy statement by the American Academy of Pediatrics said.

Adherents of Christian Science believe sickness can only be healed by spiritual understanding of biblical scripture and often refuse medical treatment for themselves and their children when they become ill.

"Pediatricians should seek to make collaborative decisions with families whenever possible and should take great care when considering seeking authority to override parental preferences," the pediatricians' statement said.

However, children have the right to appropriate medical care "when it is likely that a serious illness, injury or other medical condition endangers their lives or threatens substantial harm or suffering," the policy, published in the group's journal Pediatrics, said.

The group called for repeal of religious exemption statutes within state child abuse laws that pit a child's need for medical care against a parent's religious beliefs. "Legislation should ensure that all parents who deny their children medical care likely to prevent death or substantial harm or suffering are held legally accountable," it said.
A total of 46 of 50 states have such exemption clauses, with repeals enacted only in Hawaii, Maryland, Massachusetts and South Dakota.
